vectors.typosquat: A package named to be mistaken for a popular one
vectors.dependency-confusion: A public package hijacking the name of a private/internal one
vectors.install-script: Code that runs on install (pre/post/install scripts, trustedDependencies, curl | sh)
vectors.maintainer-takeover: Abandoned, deprecated or hijacked packages and maintainer accounts
vectors.malicious-update: A trusted package shipping a poisoned new release
vectors.leaked-secrets: Tokens and .env files exposed in the repo
vectors.remote-source: Dependencies pulled from git branches or URLs instead of the registry
vectors.ci-pipeline: Build systems, CI runners and caches
vectors.starjacking: Fake popularity: borrowed stars, inflated downloads
vectors.attack-surface: Sheer number and sprawl of dependencies

classic.q: All warfare is based on deception.
The supreme art of war is to subdue the enemy without fighting.
If you know the enemy and know yourself, you need not fear the result of a hundred battles.
Let your plans be dark and impenetrable as night, and when you move, fall like a thunderbolt.
Attack him where he is unprepared, appear where you are not expected.
The art of war teaches us to rely not on the likelihood of the enemy’s not coming, but on our own readiness to receive him.
To secure ourselves against defeat lies in our own hands, but the opportunity of defeating the enemy is provided by the enemy himself.
Rapidity is the essence of war: take advantage of the enemy’s unreadiness, make your way by unexpected routes, and attack unguarded spots.
Hold out baits to entice the enemy. Feign disorder, and crush him.
He will win who knows when to fight and when not to fight.
There is no instance of a country having benefited from prolonged warfare.
Water shapes its course according to the nature of the ground over which it flows.
O divine art of subtlety and secrecy! Through you we learn to be invisible, through you inaudible.
The victorious strategist only seeks battle after the victory has been won.
Thus, what is of supreme importance in war is to attack the enemy’s strategy.
In war, then, let your great object be victory, not lengthy campaigns.
If you know neither the enemy nor yourself, you will succumb in every battle.
If you know yourself but not the enemy, for every victory gained you will also suffer a defeat.
The good fighter is able to secure himself against defeat, but cannot make certain of defeating the enemy.
One may know how to conquer without being able to do it.
The clever combatant imposes his will on the enemy, but does not allow the enemy’s will to be imposed on him.
Whoever is first in the field and awaits the coming of the enemy, will be fresh for the fight.
Do not repeat the tactics which have gained you one victory, but let your methods be regulated by the infinite variety of circumstances.
So in war, the way is to avoid what is strong and to strike at what is weak.
Pretend to be weak, that he may grow arrogant.
Ponder and deliberate before you make a move.
Let your rapidity be that of the wind, your compactness that of the forest.
The onset of troops is like the rush of a torrent which will even roll stones along in its course.
Thus the highest form of generalship is to balk the enemy’s plans.
Knowledge of the enemy’s dispositions can only be obtained from other men.
Be subtle! be subtle! and use your spies for every kind of business.
Hostile armies may face each other for years, striving for the victory which is decided in a single day.
If it is to your advantage, make a forward move; if not, stay where you are.

apocrypha.q: The squatter waits at the crossroads wearing your friend’s name, one letter missing.
He who runs bunx on a name he cannot spell has already lost.
The impostor need not be strong. He need only be spelled like your friend after midnight.
The hyphen you forgot is the door he built.
Between the true name and the false lies the width of a thumb and the depth of a well.
The squatter does not attack your strongest package. He imitates your most beloved.
The scope protects the name, not the code.
When the public registry and the private one share a name, the louder version answers.
He who names an internal package without a scope leaves its name unguarded at the border.
The enemy publishes version ninety-nine of your secret library and waits for you to prefer the higher number.
A postinstall script is a guest who arrives carrying his own key.
The shortest README hides the longest postinstall.
A package that must reach the network to install is a soldier who first visits the enemy camp.
trustedDependencies is the list of those you have permitted to strike first.
Bun bars the gate to lifecycle scripts. Every name in trustedDependencies is a hole you cut yourself.
The installer runs before the code is read. So does the thief.
To pipe a stranger’s script into your shell is to open the gate and close your eyes.
The prebuilt binary downloaded at install is a sealed crate from a ship you never saw dock.
The maintainer who hands over the keys out of weariness hands over your house as well.
Trust no maintainer who has not been seen for three winters.
One maintainer and a million downloads: the whole army sleeps upon a single spear.
An abandoned package is a fortress with no garrison. The first to arrive holds it.
He who disables two-factor for convenience saves a minute and spends a year.
The expired domain of a maintainer’s email is a key under the doormat, sold with the house.
The kind stranger who offers to carry your burden for two years may be the burden.
A deprecated package is a general who has resigned but still wears the uniform.
The attack comes not in the version you chose, but in the patch release you accepted while sleeping.
The wise general reads the diff. The foolish general reads the changelog.
A release published at three in the morning, by a hand never seen before, deserves a candle and a long look.
Trust is earned over many versions and spent in one.
When the minified file outweighs the source, ask who else came to the feast.
Protest written into code harms the innocent first. Read before you upgrade.
He who pins his versions sleeps. He who writes the caret dreams of other men’s commits.
The lockfile is your map. Without it, the terrain shifts while you march.
‘latest’ is not a version. It is a prayer.
The caret is a door that opens toward the future. The future does not knock.
Two machines installing one package.json are two armies hearing one order in different dialects.
The star in your version field swears loyalty to every king who will ever be crowned.
Freeze the lockfile in CI, or CI will improvise.
The secret in .env is a secret only until the first commit.
The leaked token does not knock. It publishes.
The token in your .npmrc is a signet ring. Wear it; do not mail it.
Git forgets nothing. Deleting the secret in the next commit only teaches the enemy where to dig.
The library that loads your secrets must be the most boring one you own.
A secret printed once in a log is a secret told to every scribe in the empire.
A fork is a promise kept by no one.
A dependency fetched from a branch is a bridge whose planks are replaced each night.
Pin by commit, for a tag can be moved and a branch always is.
Supplies bought from a wagon by the roadside do not come with the granary’s seal.
He who audits in peace need not patch in war.
The old version you fear to upgrade is the one the enemy has studied longest.
The advisory is public. The enemy reads the news before you do.
A known flaw unpatched is not a risk. It is an invitation with a date.
The crack in your wall is already drawn on the enemy’s maps.
He who controls the build has won the battle before it is fought.
Your CI runner holds secrets it did not earn. Guard it as you would the general’s tent.
The workflow that runs on a stranger’s pull request hands him your quiver.
A cache poisoned in the night is bread poisoned for every soldier at dawn.
Inspect the vendored granary before winter, not during the famine.
A thousand stars cast no light on the code inside.
Do not fear the quiet package with no stars. Fear the loud one with stolen stars.
Popularity is a banner. Anyone may carry a banner.
The repository link in the manifest is a claim, not a proof.
The dependency you did not choose has already chosen you.
The enemy does not breach the wall. He is invited, as the dependency of a dependency of your linter.
Many small packages make a long border.
One hundred dependencies, one hundred doors. The enemy needs only one unlatched.
Every require is a bridge you have not inspected.
When the small pad falls, ten thousand builds go dark.
The helper you install for a single function brings his whole village.
Prune what you do not use. An unused dependency is a sentry who reports to no one.
The tests pass. So did the wooden horse, through the gate.
Bun is fast. The attacker is patient.
Speed is Bun’s gift. Haste is the attacker’s.
The breach is rarely clever. It is merely patient and unwatched.
Know your lockfile and know your registry, and you need not fear a hundred installs.
The guard at the gate is the first one the enemy bribes.
He who writes his own auth library writes the enemy’s victory speech.
The library that mints your sessions is the mint itself. Guard the mint.
A token that never expires is a soldier who never returns his sword.
The lock you did not forge, you must at least inspect.
Do not trust a cipher whose author you cannot name.
Randomness that is not random is a wall made of painted paper.
A wallet library that phones home has already chosen its master.
In the land of wallets, every dependency is a pickpocket’s apprentice until proven otherwise.
The address you copy is the address you trust. The clipboard trusts no one.
A request library reads every letter you send. Choose the courier carefully.
The client that follows every redirect will one day follow the enemy home.
The server middleware stands at the gate. Know which side it salutes.
Parse no URL you would not walk to on foot.
The bundler touches every line before your users do. It is the cook in your kitchen.
The plugin to your bundler is the cook’s assistant. Ask who trained him.
Dev dependencies do not ship, but they do run. On your machine. With your keys.
The tool you run once runs with all your powers. Once is enough.
The colors in your terminal were a gift. Gifts can be withdrawn.
The logger hears everything. Ensure it repeats nothing.
A log line that obeys what it writes is a scribe taking orders from the letter.
The query builder that trusts raw strings opens the gate to whoever speaks in the right tone.
The driver holds the vault’s address and the vault’s key. Few guards are trusted so much.
Ten thousand components render faithfully whatever the enemy hands them.
dangerouslySetInnerHTML was named honestly. Few read the name.
The script tag you load from a stranger’s CDN is a door to your users, not just to you.
The test runner sees your secrets in CI and asks nothing. Give it no reason to talk.
The headless browser downloads a whole army to fight a single test.
Even a package that holds only types can hold an install script.
The definition promises a shape. It does not promise a friend.
The native addon speaks the machine’s tongue. You cannot read its letters.
node-gyp builds in the dark what you will run in daylight.
The linter reads your whole army on every save. Choose a quiet companion.
The git hook runs before your judgement does.
Hash the password slowly, for the enemy guesses quickly.
The login page is the most visited gate. Its library should be the most watched.
He who invents his own cipher has invented only his own defeat.
A signing key in the repository is a seal carved on the outer wall.
The algorithm abandoned by the scholars is still welcomed in your package.json.
The chain remembers every theft forever and returns none of it.
A seed phrase in an environment variable is treasure buried beneath a signpost.
The websocket stays open long after the courtesy has ended.
The transpiler sees the code you wrote and writes the code you run. Between the two, a stranger may sit.
The update notifier calls out to the world each time you call on it.
The debug flag left on in production is a lantern hung for the enemy.
Logs shipped to a stranger’s server are diaries read aloud in the market.
The migration runs with the highest privilege and the lowest scrutiny.
The connection string is the vault’s map, key and guard’s name, written on one line.
An ORM hides the query from the general, not from the enemy.
The component library from an unknown hand renders on every screen you own.
The mock server in your tests listens on a real port.
The squatter favours @types, for no one reads a declaration.
Types are documentation that compiles. Malice also compiles.
@types/ before a name is a uniform, not an allegiance.
The binary that runs on every platform was built by someone on every platform. Do you know them all?
Configuration is the order of battle. He who changes it commands the army.
The config loader that executes its files will execute the enemy’s too.
dotenv reads your secrets faithfully. So will whoever reads dotenv.
A formatter rewrites every file you own. Grant such power sparingly.
